assets.caption: Before skinning: photograph from the collector’s preparation sequence.

assets.alt: Skinned raccoon-dog head with eyes and some muscle still present.
assets.caption: After skinning and preliminary trimming; this head is not yet fully defleshed.

assets.alt: Raccoon-dog skull lifted above a bucket containing maceration water.
assets.caption: Maceration in progress. Support the skull from below when lifting; do not use a blade as a lever through an opening.

assets.alt: Illustration of a flesh-free skull submerged in a detergent bath in an open tub.
assets.caption: AI-generated illustration of a detergent bath; not a photograph or an anatomical reference.

assets.alt: Skull held above a container of foaming whitening solution.
assets.caption: The collector’s cream-developer treatment. Foam needs headroom and secondary containment.

assets.alt: Cleaned skull, separate jaw halves, and loose teeth arranged on a dark surface.
assets.caption: Keep each specimen’s skull, jaw halves, and loose teeth together before assembly.

assets.alt: Cleaned, assembled raccoon-dog skull in an oblique view.
assets.caption: After cleaning and assembly: retain natural bone texture rather than chasing a uniform white finish.
